name: Why Is One Kitchen Remodeling Bid Much Lower Than Another in Apollo Beach?

mainEntity.name: Why is one written kitchen remodeling estimate much lower than the others in Apollo Beach?
mainEntity.text: Why is one written kitchen remodeling estimate much lower than the others in Apollo Beach?

acceptedAnswer.text: A large price difference usually means the proposals are based on different assumptions. The lowest Apollo Beach estimate may omit cabinet installation, electrical upgrades, plumbing adjustments, delivery, disposal, drywall repair, painting, permits, inspections, or final cleanup. It may also use lower material allowances or exclude labor for work described elsewhere as an allowance. Place each estimate in a side-by-side table and mark whether it includes demolition, floor protection, cabinet fillers, finished panels, trim, countertop templating, sink installation, appliance connections, lighting, ventilation, patching, painting, waste removal, and permit coordination. Ask the contractor to explain every blank, lump-sum line, and unusually low allowance. Request a revised estimate that uses identical products and scope. Also compare the contractor’s schedule, project supervision, warranty, insurance, references, and change-order procedure. A low bid can become expensive if hidden conditions are handled through frequent changes or if finish work is left incomplete. Do not assume the highest bid is best either; evaluate completeness and clarity. The strongest proposal explains what will happen, who will perform it, what it costs, and what could legitimately change the price.
acceptedAnswer.description: A low estimate may exclude permits, demolition, disposal, labor, finish work, or realistic material allowances. It may also assume fewer repairs or a smaller project scope. Compare every line item, allowance, exclusion, warranty, and payment term before treating the lower total as a savings.
